name: AudioContext rendering fingerprint
plain: Renders a silent tone through an audio graph offline and sums the output samples.
meaning: Tiny floating point differences in the audio stack (DynamicsCompressor, oscillator math, CPU SIMD) give a number that is stable per browser build and hardware. It never plays sound.

steps: Sum abs of a slice of the Float32Array

data.metric: Sum of about 500 samples, 15 digit float

fields.name: fingerprint sum
fields.precision: varies at the 1e-14 level by browser

limits.headline: Can run a silent sound test and turn the result into a device number
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Render a quiet tone in memory and add up the results
Turn those tiny differences into one repeatable number
Match that number across visits, even with cookies cleared
cannot: Work the same way in Brave, Safari 26 and Firefox private mode, which add noise
limits.differs: Brave, Firefox in strict or private mode and Safari 26 add noise to the result. Chrome and Edge do not.

story.what_it_is: A script plays a silent tone through a sound chain offline and adds up the numbers to make an ID.
story.for_you: Nothing you can see or hear happens. Your device does a small math job, and the answer is nearly the same every time, so it can recognize you without cookies.
story.for_makers: It is one of the classic fingerprinting tricks. It needs no permission and adds extra bits to a visitor ID. Fraud teams like it because it survives cookie clearing and private windows in some browsers.

use_cases.example: An ad broker links your visits across unrelated sites by checking the same audio result each time.
A login page compares the audio result to the one stored when you set up the account, and asks for more proof if it differs.
A site counting unique visitors uses it to tell apart two people on the same office network.
A shop spots one person making hundreds of accounts to abuse a coupon, because the audio result matches.
A game with a free trial limit stops people from creating new accounts again and again on the same device.
A bank adds the audio result to its device recognition so a stolen password alone is not enough.
A social site finds the same person behind a fake follower network using shared device traits.

risks: Hard to avoid without breaking audio
Privacy browsers add noise on purpose

technical_bounds: Mostly identifies browser and OS build, not individual devices
Same hardware with same browser collides

value.abuse: Cheap fingerprint component that survives cookie clearing

history.change: Englehardt and Narayanan find audio fingerprinting scripts on the web
Web Audio readback noise in Private Browsing
Noise extended to all browsing for known fingerprinting scripts
